rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.graph.search.group_hits` has no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence, and it has no implementation edges. Each clause describes observable behaviour:

- "Deliver one entry per enclosing item in a text search, even when the item has several hits." This concerns the number of entries returned. Any implementation that returns one entry per item behaves the same, whether it groups with a map, a sort-and-merge or a streaming pass.
- "Group before pagination so an item's excerpt stays together." This is an ordering constraint on results. Page contents and sizes show it, and no named library, algorithm or interface is required.
- "Each entry carries a node reference ..., one excerpt, and the page-local tag used by `finish_search`." This describes what the output contains. It does not prescribe a Rust type, field names or a signature. The node reference's form is defined by the cited `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`, which only supplies context. A differently declared entry type that renders the same fields would still conform.

None of these clauses fixes how the code is built, so Success is correct with no roots. How well tests cover the behaviour is a separate question and is not judged here.

behavioral: The two marked tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.group_hits`.

- **One entry per enclosing item, even with several hits.** `search_groups_exact_occurrences_and_records_the_selected_declaration` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs` searches `const A … "éhit"; const B … "hit hit"`. It checks that the raw search returns three hits: one in `const[A]` and two in `const[B]`. It then asserts that the `search_text` page has exactly two entries, with `const[B]`'s two hits merged into one entry whose excerpt is `const B: &str = "hit hit";`.
- **Group before pagination, so an item's excerpt stays together.** `search_pages_return_every_original_match_in_order` writes 350 lines of `hit N hit`, so each line has two hits. It pages through the whole result and asserts that each entry exactly equals `{node, file, selector, excerpt: lines[count], tag}` in order. It also asserts that the entry count equals 350 and that there is more than one page. A split item would show up as an extra or duplicated entry. The `search_text` dispatch code I read in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#impl[Session<'_, D>/ToolSession<D>]/fn[dispatch]` builds the groups from the full hit list before it builds the entries that get paged.
- **Each entry carries a node reference, one excerpt and a page-local tag.** Both tests assert the exact JSON of every entry, including `node`, `file`, `selector`, `excerpt` and `tag`. The pagination test asserts that tags restart at `"1"` on every page (`index+1`). The `node_reference` requirement is cited context, and the grouping test uses the entry's `node` when it reads the item.
- **The tag accounts for use of the excerpt.** The grouping test calls `finish_search` with `used: []` and expects no dependencies. It calls it again with `used: ["2"]` and expects a dependency on `const[B]` with the item's fingerprint.
- **The node reference lets the agent read the full item.** The grouping test calls `session.read_node` on the second entry. It asserts that the resulting dependency is the `const[B]` node.

I found no unacknowledged gap, and no further test markers are needed.

text: Deliver one entry per enclosing item in a text search, even when the item has several hits. Group before pagination so an item's excerpt stays together. Each entry carries a node reference under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`, one excerpt, and the page-local tag used by `finish_search`. The tag accounts for use of the excerpt. The node reference lets the agent read the full item.

The harness represents a `NodeId<D>` as an unsigned integer. Each built-in tool that accepts a node accepts the same top-level address fields, alongside its own arguments (such as an edge `label`). `NodeAddress` in tool signatures denotes these alternatives:
| `node` | Look up the assigned ID in the domain's cache. |

| `path`, optional `location` | Resolve the project-relative file within the domain's visible sources. `location` is its outline selector and defaults to the empty selector for the file root. Resolve the item, map its `OutlineData` through `Domain::source_node`, and intern the resulting identity. |
| `data` | Deserialize the JSON value as `D::NodeData` and intern it in the domain's cache. |

For domains using the agent harness, the tool schema describes `data` using the domain’s JSON schema for `D::NodeData`. The harness uses the same JSON representation when returning and accepting an identity.

Resolving an address is discovery. The requested operation determines which observations enter evidence. Invalid addresses, unavailable files, and unknown selectors produce tool errors before the requested operation runs.
